meta.subtitle: Dual-port 25GbE bonding: Server A (172.16.12.131) <-> Server B (172.16.13.108)
meta.platform: Server A: AMD EPYC 9124 (251 GiB)  /  Server B: AMD EPYC 9745 (1.5 TiB) -- back-to-back

executive_summary: Validation and benchmark of dual-port 25G NIC performance with and without NIC bonding (link aggregation) between two servers, back-to-back over SFP28 25G-SR fibre (no switch) with jumbo frames. Throughput from iperf3, latency from qperf/ping, across single-link and bonded configurations (balance-rr and balance-xor).

A single 25G link is healthy: ~24 Gb/s (B->A), ~17 Gb/s (A->B), ~18 us latency, near-zero loss with jumbo frames. There is a consistent directional asymmetry (receive-path / CPU contention on the busy Kubernetes node A).

Bonding did not cleanly double throughput - but the cause is the host platform, not the NIC: one of Server A's 25G cards sits in a PCIe x4 slot (31.5 Gb/s) and the only stable two-link bond forced both A ports onto that card, capping aggregate ~31 Gb/s and causing RX loss on B->A; several inter-server fibre links were also marginal (RS-FEC off, mixed optics). balance-rr is unsuitable for TCP (heavy reordering).

rows: Capped by host PCIe x4 slot + marginal optics (not a NIC fault)

cpu.model: Server A: AMD EPYC 9124 (16C/64T)  |  Server B: AMD EPYC 9745 (128C/512T)

memory.total: Server A 251 GiB  |  Server B 1.5 TiB

comparison.caption: Directional throughput across configurations (iperf3, MTU 9000).
comparison.notes: B->A leads on a single link, but bonded B->A degrades because both of Server A's bonded ports share one PCIe x4 slot (RX-side loss). Latency: single-link 18 us (qperf TCP) / 0.45 ms ping; under bond 24 us / 0.52 ms.

dmesg_status: balance-rr produced tens of thousands of TCP retransmissions (packet reordering) -- unsuitable for TCP. Repeated bond reconfiguration stressed the bnxt_en driver and briefly hung Server B's network stack (self-recovered, no reboot).
findings: A single 25G link is healthy: ~24 Gb/s (B->A), ~17 Gb/s (A->B), ~18 us latency, near-zero loss with jumbo frames.
Directional asymmetry: A->B consistently ~17 Gb/s vs B->A ~24 Gb/s per link (receive-path / CPU contention on the busy Kubernetes node A).

Bonding did not cleanly double throughput due to host constraints: (a) one of Server A's 25G cards is in a PCIe x4 slot (31.5 Gb/s) and the only stable two-link bond forced both A ports onto it -- capping ~31G and causing RX loss on B->A; (b) several inter-server fibre links were marginal (RS-FEC off, mixed optics).
balance-rr (round-robin) is unsuitable for TCP -- heavy reordering and tens of thousands of retransmissions with no real gain.
Repeated bond reconfiguration stressed the bnxt driver and briefly hung Server B's network stack (self-recovered, no reboot).
recommendations: Move Server A's 25G card from the PCIe x4 slot into an x8 slot (or bond one port per card across two x8 cards) -- the single biggest blocker to real 2x25G aggregation.
Use matching 25G-SR optics on both ends of every link, clean/reseat the LC connectors, and enable RS-FEC (ethtool --set-fec <dev> encoding rs).
For production bonding, prefer 802.3ad (LACP) via a switch over back-to-back, and persist the configuration in netplan once links are stable.
Use balance-xor or 802.3ad (flow hashing) for TCP -- never balance-rr.
Expected after the above: ~45-48 Gb/s multi-flow aggregate on a 2x25G bond.

rows: Both 25G NICs link at 25 Gb/s; jumbo stable, 0% loss
Bond forms and carries traffic in both modes
Capped by host PCIe x4 slot + marginal optics (not a NIC fault)
